source: This might be due to crowding around the 5-fold symmetry axes, which reduces the variability in the heterodimer position.

claim: The distance between the carboxy end of one domain and the amino end of the next domain prior to regularization did not exceed 6.9 Å (excluding the flexible domain B), indicating that the quality of fit was reasonable.

source: Comparison of the hinge angles between domains in the four quasi-equivalent positions (Table 3) did not exceed 13°, except for defining the orientation of the B domain in E2.

claim: Considering that the length of the longest domain (DII of E1) is about 50 Å, a 13° hinge angle difference implies a relative difference of about 6 Å for atoms furthest from the hinge, corresponding to a maximum movement of about three standard deviations between superimposed structures.
source: Considering that the length of the longest domain (DII of E1) is about 50 Å, this implies a relative difference of about 6 Å for atoms furthest from the hinge, corresponding to a maximum movement of about three standard deviations between superimposed structures.

source: The shape and size of the carbohydrate moiety for each of the three N-linked glycosylation sites is consistent in each of the four quasi-equivalent positions.

claim: The centers of the carbohydrate moieties were ∼6 Å from the N atom of the glycosylated Asn residues.
source: The centers of the carbohydrate moieties were ∼6 Å from the N atom of the glycosylated Asn residues.

source: The E1 and E2 glycoproteins that form the four heterodimers in the VLPs have more contacts with each other in the independently fitted structure than in the crystallographic heterodimer structure.

source: Thus, the i3 trimers in the VLPs were more compact with a greater number of interactions between its component molecules than the q3 trimer.

source: At the top of the spike, the i3 and q3 spikes showed less difference.

source: Thus, in comparison with the 20 i3 spikes, the 60 q3 spikes may be poised to release the E2 molecules from the center of the spikes in preparation for the formation of the E1 fusogenic homotrimers early in the infection (Li et al., 2010).

source: In the CHIK VLP structure, His170 (equivalent to SINV His 169) does not interact closely with other negatively charged residues that would be required for a pH-sensing switch whereas CHIKV His 256 (equivalent to SINV His256) contacts Glu166.

claim: A homology model for CHIKV NCP (residues 119 to 267) was generated based on the crystal structure of the SFV NCP.
source: Therefore, a homology model for CHIKV NCP (residues 119 to 267) was generated based on the crystal structure of the SFV NCP (Protein Data Bank accession number 1VCP).

source: The orientation and placement of the homology NCP in the cryoEM density was essentially the same as described for other alphaviruses (Zhang et al., 2002).

claim: Contrary to the organization of the E1-E2 glycoproteins, where there are extensive inter-heterodimer contacts within the trimeric spikes, there were few contacts among the three NCP molecules around the icosahedral 3-fold axes and no contacts among the three NCP molecules around the quasi-3-fold axes.
source: Contrary to the organization of the E1-E2 glycoproteins, where there are extensive inter-heterodimer contacts within the trimeric spikes, there were few contacts among the three NCP molecules around the icosahedral 3-fold axes and no contacts among the three NCP molecules around the quasi-3-fold axes.

source: Moreover, salt bridges were formed between Lys178 and Glu240.

claim: It was unexpected that the positions of the quasi-2- and 3-fold symmetry elements were matched almost perfectly between the external organization of the glycoproteins into 80 trimers and the internal organization of the NCP into 12 pentamers and 30 hexamers.
source: It was unexpected that the positions of the quasi-2- and 3-fold symmetry elements were matched almost perfectly between the external organization of the glycoproteins into 80 trimers and the internal organization of the NCP into 12 pentamers and 30 hexamers (Figure 2).

claim: The nucleoplasmic cores assemble in the cytoplasm and are transported to the plasma membrane where they interact with the endodomain of the E2 protein.
source: The nucleoplasmic cores assemble in the cytoplasm (Weiss et al., 1989; Owen and Kuhn, 1996; Soonsawad et al., 2010) and are transported to the plasma membrane where they interact with the endodomain of the E2 protein.
evidence: This describes the assembly pathway, supported by citations.

claim: The interaction between the nucleoplasmic cores and E2 endodomain provides an opportunity for the C-terminal regions of E2 to bind to the hydrophobic pocket on the surface of the nucleocapsid, thus nucleating the E1-E2 glycoproteins to form an icosahedral shell in synchrony with the icosahedral symmetry of the cores.
source: This provides an opportunity for the C-terminal regions of E2 to bind to the hydrophobic pocket on the surface of the nucleocapsid (Lee et al., 1996), thus nucleating the E1-E2 glycoproteins to form an icosahedral shell in synchrony with the icosahedral symmetry of the cores.

claim: Cα models were built of the missing part of the E1-E2 ectodomains, the TM helices, and the E2 endodomain, based on Rosetta structural predictions and on the cryoEM density.
source: Cα models were built of the missing part of the E1-E2 ectodomains, the TM helices, and the E2 endodomain, based on Rosetta structural predictions (Lange and Baker, 2012) and on the cryoEM density.

claim: The alignment of the amino acid sequence with the cryoEM density was based on assigning the kink observed in the TM helix of E1 to the likely flexible Thr-Gly-Gly sequence.
source: The alignment of the amino acid sequence with the cryoEM density was based on assigning the kink observed in the TM helix of E1 to the likely flexible Thr-Gly-Gly sequence.

source: The E1 and E2 helices were parallel and situated close together with some hydrophobic contacts between them (Table 6).

claim: Although the lipid membrane is presumably flexible and likely to have different organization of lipid molecules in different particles, the cryoEM density showed a preference for roughly radial density features.
source: Although the lipid membrane is presumably flexible and likely to have different organization of lipid molecules in different particles, the cryoEM density showed a preference for roughly radial density features.

source: Presumably, these densities represent an average of similarly placed lipid molecules, as was observed in the 4 Å resolution X-ray crystallographic map of the dsDNA PRD1 bacteriophage (Cockburn et al., 2004).

claim: The overall radius of VEEV and CHIK VLPs is essentially the same.
source: This shows that the overall radius of these two viruses is essentially the same.

claim: The positions and orientations of the molecular protein components have changed by up to 9.7 Å and 11.7°, respectively, between VEEV and CHIK VLPs.
source: However, the positions and orientations of the molecular protein components have changed by up to 9.7 Å and 11.7°, respectively (Table 8), which is far greater than the RMS Cα atom differences between quasi equivalent positions of the component molecular components in the CHIK VLPs (maximum RMS distance is 2.4 Å, Table 4).

claim: The change in molecular positions and orientation with respect to the icosahedral framework between VEEV and CHIK VLPs is highly significant.
source: Thus the change in molecular positions and orientation with respect to the icosahedral framework is highly significant.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the structural comparison.

claim: Although the capsid protein amino acids are more conserved than any of the other structural proteins, by far the largest differences in position and orientation of the molecular components occur for the capsid proteins.
source: Although the capsid protein amino acids are more conserved than any of the other structural proteins (Table 8), by far the largest differences in position and orientation of the molecular components occur for the capsid proteins (Table 8).

claim: The greater conservation of the amino acid sequences for the capsid protein is reflected in a lower RMS differences between Cα atoms between superimposed capsid structures of VEEV and CHIK VLPs (less than 1.2 Å) as opposed to a comparison of the other molecular components (greater than 2.0 Å).
source: The greater conservation of the amino acid sequences for the capsid protein is also reflected in a lower RMS differences between Cα atoms between superimposed capsid structures of VEEV and CHIK VLPs (less than 1.2 Å) as opposed to a comparison of the other molecular components (greater than 2.0 Å, Table 8).

claim: These two alpha-viruses maintain a fairly constant tertiary structure, notwithstanding moderate amino acid sequence variations.
source: The above analysis shows that these two alpha-viruses maintain a fairly constant tertiary structure, notwithstanding moderate amino acid sequence variations.

claim: The quaternary organization has greater variability between VEEV and CHIK VLPs, although still retaining the same T = 4 quasi symmetry.
source: However, the quaternary organization has greater variability, although still retaining the same T = 4 quasi symmetry.
evidence: This is a conclusion about quaternary structure differences.

claim: Four cryoEM structures were determined to ∼15 Å resolution of CHIK VLPs complexed with the Fab fragments of the neutralizing mouse MAbs CHK-9, CHK-152, m242 and m10.
source: Four cryoEM structures were determined to ∼15 Å resolution of CHIK VLPs complexed with the Fab fragments of the neutralizing mouse MAbs CHK-9, CHK-152, m242 and m10 (Figure 4).

claim: All Fab fragments bound the VLPs with one Fab fragment per E2 molecule.
source: All Fab fragments bound the VLPs with one Fab fragment per E2 molecule.

source: Except for CHK-152, the concentration of the Fab molecules required for 50% neutralization was 100 or more times greater than the intact IgG (Figure 5).

source: This implies a fundamental difference between how CHK-152 binds to the VLPs compared to the other Fabs.

source: Because CHK-152 MAb and Fab fragment neutralize CHIKV at almost the same low concentration, it is unlikely that this MAb requires bivalent binding to inhibit infection.

claim: The coordinates of the E2 B domain in the VLPs did not agree well with the B domain density in the maps of the VLP complexed with the CHK-9 or m242 Fab fragments, suggesting that the E2 B domain had a different orientation in these Fab-bound structures than in the non-complexed VLPs.
source: The coordinates of the E2 B domain in the VLPs did not agree well with the B domain density in the maps of the VLP complexed with the CHK-9 or m242 Fab fragments, suggesting that the E2 B domain had a different orientation in these Fab-bound structures than in the non-complexed VLPs.

source: The crystal structures of CHK-9 and m242 Fab fragments were determined to 3.0 Å and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively (Table 9).

source: VLP-CHK-152 and VLP-m10 Fab cryoEM maps were best fitted with the Fab structures of CHK-9 and of m242, respectively (Figure 6).

source: The density for the constant domains (remote from the VLPs) of the Fab fragments was about 17% lower, consistent with the flexibility of the elbow angle between the constant and variable domains.

source: The footprint of CHK-9 and m242 Fabs onto the VLP localized primarily onto the domain A and did not include any part of domain B.

source: Indeed, binding of these fragments to the VLPs had nudged domain B ∼10 Å sideways, out of the way of the Fab fragment (Figure 7).

source: The footprint of CHK-152, however, spanned both domains B and A as well as the linker peptides to domain B represented by domain D.

source: Thus, unlike the other Fabs, CHK-152 has the capacity to cross-link domain B with domain A.

source: Alphaviruses become fusogenic at low pH when domain B, held in place by the flexible β-ribbons of domain D, becomes mobile and exposes the fusion loop on domain II of E1.

source: As CHK-152 efficiently blocks viral fusion with host membranes (P Pal and M Diamond, unpublished observations), it may do so by cross-linking the flexible domain B to the rest of the virus surface.

source: An analogous mechanism of inhibition was described for neutralization of West Nile virus, in which the viral envelope proteins were cross-linked by the bound FAB fragments (Kaufmann et al., 2010).

source: All four MAbs examined here bind to the end of the trimeric spikes that includes the putative receptor attachment region (Davis et al., 1991; Dubuisson and Rice, 1993; Kinney et al., 1993; Klimstra et al., 1998; Bernard et al., 2000; Lee et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2003; Pierro et al., 2007, 2008; Ryman et al., 2007; Li et al., 2010), although only the CHK-9 Fab footprint actually overlaps the site (Figure 7).

source: Nevertheless the proximity of these footprints to the possible receptor-binding site could probably allow neutralization by competitively limiting access of the virus to the cell surface receptor.

source: To block formation of a fusogenic E1 trimer it is necessary to bind a Fab molecule to only one of the three E2 molecules in every spike.

source: Such a stoichiometry would require substantially higher concentrations of Fabs to inhibit infectivity, as seen with CHK-9, m10 and m242 Fabs (Figure 5).

source: In summary our structural studies suggest that the CHK-9, m10, and m242 Fab fragments neutralize CHIKV infectivity by blocking the cellular binding site on the A domain of E2 and that the CHK152 inhibits fusion by stabilizing domain B of E2, preventing exposure of the fusion loop on E1.

claim: CHK152 inhibits fusion by stabilizing domain B of E2, preventing exposure of the fusion loop on E1.

source: CHIK VLPs have been reported as structural and immunologically indistinguishable from the mature infectious virus (Akahata et al., 2010); the use of CHIKV VLPs instead of live infectious virus has allowed us to avoid performing all structural studies under biosafety level 3 conditions.

claim: The use of CHIKV VLPs instead of live infectious virus has allowed the researchers to avoid performing all structural studies under biosafety level 3 conditions.
source: CHIK VLPs have been reported as structural and immunologically indistinguishable from the mature infectious virus (Akahata et al., 2010); the use of CHIKV VLPs instead of live infectious virus has allowed us to avoid performing all structural studies under biosafety level 3 conditions.
